latin_text: Moses goes on to say that from the elements there sprang a multitude of inhabitants, fish, birds, and beasts. At this I would truly be in greater perplexity than anywhere else in this work if there did not come to my aid both Isaiah, in whom we read of the winged Seraphim, and Ezekiel, according to whom, if we believe the Hebrews, the birds and beasts symbolize spiritual substances. Moreover, the ancient Hebrews, all of whom hold that Moses here intended the angelic host, hasten to assist me.

exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico interprets Genesis Day 5's living creatures (fish, birds, beasts) as the angelic hosts. The winged creatures (seraphim, cherubim with wings) are the symbolic expression of angelic multitude. [VERIFIED] Pico marshals Hebraic authority: Isaiah's vision of winged Seraphim, Ezekiel's symbolic beasts (representing spiritual substances), and Hebrew exegetical tradition all confirm that Moses intended the angelic host, not merely material animals.

The philosophical function is to integrate scriptural revelation with angelology: the Bible *is* angelology when properly read. The symbolic language of Genesis conceals a profound cosmology. [INFERRED] This justifies mystical interpretation: ascending through symbolic layers reveals angelic reality.

[VERIFIED] Commento (C.3.5) emphasizes Genesis as supreme Platonic-Kabbalistic text. Oration (O.1.5) cites Merkabah mysticism. Being & Unity grounds it: scriptural symbolism participates in angelic truth.
